passage: Kunal was two and a half when he threw his cup, shoved his plate away and wailed at everything, even the toy he had asked for. His mother Preeti looked at the clock. Lunch was an hour late. She sat him down with warm rice and dal, and he ate in silence, sniffing. Ten minutes later he was laughing at a spoon. At fifteen, Kunal came home after a long practice snapping at everyone. His sister Rajni asked how his day went and he glared at her. Then he stopped and said, "Sorry. Let me eat something first, then we talk." He made two chapattis, ate them at the counter, and afterwards told her about the match. At twenty-five, Kunal skipped lunch to finish a report. By four o'clock he had typed a curt email to a colleague and read his own draft with cold certainty that his job was going nowhere. He texted Rajni, "Nothing I do here matters." She replied with a single line: "Have you eaten today? 🙂" He looked at the empty lunch box on his desk and went to the canteen.

qa.q: What did Kunal say to his sister after his practice at fifteen?
qa.a: He said, "Sorry. Let me eat something first, then we talk."

qa.q: How do Kunal's moods at two and a half, fifteen and twenty-five connect to food?
qa.a: At two and a half he threw his cup and wailed because lunch was an hour late, at fifteen he snapped after practice until he ate, and at twenty-five skipping lunch made a report feel hopeless and his email curt. Each time he calmed once he ate, though only at fifteen did he notice the pattern himself.

qa.q: What was Kunal feeling when he texted Rajni that nothing he did there mattered?
qa.a: He felt hopeless and discouraged, and his empty stomach made the work look bigger and worse than it was. 😔

qa.q: What could Kunal do at work to avoid skipping meals when a deadline is close?
qa.a: He could set a time to eat before he starts on the report and keep a snack at his desk, so a low mood does not decide his emails.

grounding: The same person's mood tracks low fuel at three ages: a hungry toddler's tantrum, a teenager who learns to eat before talking, and an adult whose skipped lunch turns a report hopeless.
